### VIII

Likewise, a copy of the charter which the lord Domnolus made from the estate called Canon, with the consent of his canons, for the church of Saint Vincent.

In the twentieth year of the reign of our most glorious lord King Chilperic, on the day before the Nones of September, I, Domnolus, bishop in the name of Christ, having summoned my lord and brother Audoveus, bishop of the city of Angers, to visit the holy thresholds of the shrine of my own patron, Bishop Victorius, and having solemnly celebrated his feast, with the consent of all my brother presbyters, declare that, since I formerly composed my testament but have not yet fulfilled my intention therein, what appears to have been written by me I wish to be preserved in every respect, and I desire that this little charter receive full force.

I give to the basilica of Saints Vincent and Laurence, which I built and constructed by my own labor and established for the salvation of the city and the people, the estate called Canon, with its fields, meadows, pastures, woods, waters and courses of waters, and two slaves: Waldard with his wife and their children, who are now seen to dwell there. From this day forward, let the aforesaid abbot of the aforesaid place recall them to provide the support of the brothers of the basilica called by that name; and nevertheless, after my death, when God commands,

[scan page 26, continuation]

let whoever is ordained there from the aforesaid place ensure that my commemoration is fulfilled every year.

Therefore, to you, Niviard, deacon and defender of our church, I declare and command that, by your delivery, you cause this property, just as it is now possessed by the said church, together with all its entirety and appurtenances, to be handed over to Abbot Suolevus.

I asked that this also be inserted, so that whoever should oppose my will may incur that curse which the Prophet sang in Psalm 109, and so that this present charter may remain unshaken. For the truth of the matter I have subscribed it with my own hand and asked that it be secured by my lords and brothers.

Domnolus the sinner subscribed. Audoveus the sinner subscribed at the request of the lord Domnolus, bishop. Theoduifus the sinner subscribed. Aimulfus the presbyter subscribed. Leudoricus the presbyter subscribed.

### IX

It was also deemed appropriate to include in this little work a copy of the imperial charter which the aforesaid Aldric received from the lord Louis, the most pious emperor, when he succeeded in having the property of the aforesaid abbey of Saint Vincent, together with the abbey itself, adjudicated and assigned to him.

This charter: see *Patrologia*, volume CIV, column 1217, among the diplomas of Louis the Pious.

### X

Likewise, in this document, or in this little book, it was deemed appropriate to insert a copy of the charter which the aforesaid lord Aldric succeeded in receiving concerning the estate called Brogilus or Novavilla, with everything belonging to it, both small estates and slaves, as well as little properties and forests, and also everything lawfully belonging to them, so that, if necessary, this copy may appear to the faithful of the aforesaid Church in times to come, and so that the matter in question may be known to all.

(See above, column 1218.)

### XI

Moreover, in this work it seemed appropriate to inscribe a copy of the charter which the aforesaid Aldric received concerning the offerings and tithes, the restorations of churches, and the revenues both of monasteries and of cells and estates, which, through royal grants, the king’s vassals had succeeded in acquiring—although unjustly and contrary to canonical authority.

For the offerings of the faithful are to be distributed and administered by bishops and their ministers according to canonical institution, not by lay or secular persons; those laymen who presume to do so are severely struck by the holy Fathers under the name of anathema. They too must take great care lest, for temporal things belonging to this age, they become perpetually alienated from the delights of the heavenly kingdom—which God forbid.

(The charter in question: see above, column 1219.)

### XII

It was also deemed appropriate to insert in this writing copies of the charters which the aforesaid lord Aldric, bishop of the aforesaid city, received concerning the little monastery of Saint Mary situated within the walls of the city and beside the river Sarthe,

[scan page 27]

Aldric

43

which the most pious lord Louis, emperor, out of love of God and reverence for the saints, and also because of his affection and love for the aforesaid Aldric, bishop of the aforesaid city, duly and legally transferred to the mother and senior church of the city.

The aforesaid lord Aldric renewed, solemnly consecrated, and reconciled it in honor of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ and of his mother Mary, as well as of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius and Saint Stephen. He deserved to consecrate that church solemnly and with the greatest care in memory of the aforesaid saints, with many bishops and priests, nobles, and other ministers of Christ and of the holy Church of God assembled, with the agreement, namely, of the many absent and innumerable noble bishops.

At first he received this charter because he thought that the aforesaid little monastery was a royal donation and part of the emperors’ fisc. But after he discovered, by searching the traditions, precarias, privileges, and instruments of many charters in the archive of the aforesaid church, that the aforesaid monastery of Saint Mary had been transferred to the aforesaid mother and city church by devout and free men and women of noble rank, he received another charter, as it is inserted therein.

For this reason he took care to do this, so that, if—God forbid—some dispute should arise from this in future times, and if the aforesaid charters should be taken away or lost by some device, copies of both might be found in these documents of the charters, and might be inserted in this little book, so that the officials of the aforesaid see and church, should necessity arise, might be able through them to obtain assistance and recovery.

(See above, columns 1259 and 1256.)

### XIII

It is also necessary to insert here a copy of the charter which the aforesaid lord Aldric received concerning the properties, monasteries, cells, villages, and separately named estates, under the protection and administration of the immunity of his see and church, which he rebuilt, almost reconstructed anew, improved, and enlarged, and which he solemnly consecrated in honor of the holy Lord and Savior, of blessed Mary, his mother, and of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, as well as Saint Stephen.

He deserved to receive the charter represented by this copy from the most pious emperor, the lord Louis, as it is contained and inserted therein. For this is how it is written there.

(See above, column 1257.)

### XIV

It was therefore also deemed appropriate to insert the aforesaid charters in this work so that, as has been said, if any question should arise in future or in the present concerning the aforesaid properties, copies of the aforementioned charters might be found inserted in this little book, so that through these copies the faithful and the rectors and governors of the aforesaid church might obtain assistance.

For the aforesaid lord Aldric, bishop of the aforementioned city, took care to receive certain other charters for the sake of security, which, because of their length, or because of the weariness of those listening or reading, or because of the tedium imposed on the writers, he did not at all wish to insert in these documents.

### XV

The aforesaid Aldric, bishop of the aforementioned city, also collected certain chapters of the canons, very useful and necessary, which he assigned to his fellow priests to be read or committed to memory very frequently.

The preface of his work states that he caused these chapters to be gathered in brief from the canons and decrees of the Fathers. First, he collected several chapters from twelve councils and from the decrees of the bishops of the Roman see, placing their preface at the very beginning of the work as something extremely useful.

Then he collected what follows from other canonical collections and from the sayings of the Fathers of various provinces. With some of the holiest and most learned bishops he also enacted several of these matters in synods, as well as from the chapters of the most Christian emperors and from the decrees of bishops in synods, both in the time of Pippin and of Charles and Louis, as can be found by diligent investigators in the prefaces of this little book.

The aforesaid Bishop Aldric also made a structure called a ciborium over the principal altar, which is consecrated, as has been specified, in honor of the Lord and Savior, of holy Mary, the mother of God, and of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, as well as Saint Stephen, and likewise in veneration and honor of all the saints.

He took care to fashion that ciborium wonderfully in silver, as it appears today; and he ordered silver and gilded crowns to be affixed above it, as the work still appears to those who behold it.

In that place where formerly dogs, prostitutes, and robbers used to dwell, he built a monastery above the river Sarthe, a mile and a half distant from the aforesaid city, in honor of the holy Savior, of holy Mary, the mother of God, and of the holy martyrs Stephen, Gervasius, and Protasius, and of all the saints. In it he also had a new dormitory carefully constructed, and in that dormitory he built an apse wonderfully on the eastern side; in it he built and raised an altar.

He solemnly consecrated that apse, together with the aforesaid altar, on the fourth day before the Ides of September, with its relics, in honor of Saint Benedict, the principal confessor. Where formerly the barking of dogs and the howling of the poor—who had been despoiled by the robbers dwelling there—resounded, he established that angelic and prophetic hymns, or the praises of the other divine Scriptures, should be sung and resound to the Lord day and night.

He also built in that monastery a new and nobly arranged refectory, and constructed the other workshops of the brothers, both storerooms and other workshops, wonderfully and suitably; he organized them according to the rule and assigned them to the monks for habitation. In that place he began to lay and construct the foundations of the church and cloister.

[scan page 28]

This work revealed great divine power, because what many thought could not be completed in two or three years was, with the Lord’s assistance, completed in four years and five and a half months; that is, from the Kalends of March to the sixteenth day before the Kalends of October. On the day of the Kalends the church was consecrated, and the monks there newly found sleep in the dormitory and eat in the refectory.

This could in no way have happened unless the Lord’s mercies and his great power had accomplished the work. Therefore he too is praised, because he was deemed worthy to perform, grant, and accomplish this through divine agency. To him be honor and glory throughout the ages of ages. Amen.

### XVI

In the aforesaid monastery he built anew a church wonderfully and orderly arranged. In it he raised fourteen altars and dedicated and consecrated them in honor of the saints whose names are recorded below; he placed relics in them. Their names are written in the following manner:

The whole church, as has been stated, was solemnly and fittingly consecrated in honor of the Lord and Savior, of his holy mother Mary, the mother of God, and of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius and Saint Stephen, and likewise in honor of all the saints, on the fourth day before the Kalends of October.

While the consecration of the aforesaid church was being carried out by the aforementioned bishop and his ministers, a remarkable event occurred, not to be concealed. A certain man came—[the text is corrupt here; apparently “moved by the exhortation of men or by a call”]. But, inspired by divine clemency and moved to contrition, a man named Salahardus, of noble birth, came to the aforesaid place, to the aforesaid bishop, and to the congregation.

He said that he wished to give his own property to the same devotion and to the aforesaid place, and to deliver his two sons to the aforesaid church in servitude, so that, if it pleased the Lord, they might become monks and serve the Lord there throughout all the days of their lives.

This was done after the consecration of the aforesaid oratory, with the Lord’s consent. The aforementioned man therefore transferred, in the presence of many noble bystanders, to the aforesaid bishop, together with his priests and monks, who were standing above the aforesaid altar of the holy Savior and receiving the vow, as much of his own property as he could transfer for twelve solidi of gold [text corrupt].

Therefore, he made a charter for the aforesaid bishop, his priests, and the monks serving the Lord there, and noble and religious men acted as witnesses to the same property and deed.

Thus this remarkable event occurred, if God has shown it to us in the manner in which we have been able to set it down. For this reason we have inserted it here, so that all the servants of God may pray for those who, through their vows to the Lord, have begun to increase, magnify, and fulfill his service.

### XVII

After the consecration had been solemnly completed, he consecrated the church in honor of the aforementioned saints and, for the support of the brothers serving the Lord there, together with his fellow bishops and the clerics living holy lives, and with the consultation and consent of all the clergy and people, he transferred four splendidly written Gospels and a golden chalice with its paten.

For he transferred that Gospel-book and the aforesaid golden chalice, consecrated to God, while the other bishops and fellow priests laid their hands upon them and all the rest consented and prayed. He transferred them there, from the property of his own see and church, with the counsel of all, in the presence of many noble and free men who stood by as witnesses.

These were: the estate of Apiacum, where Saint Ulfacius, confessor of Christ, rests bodily, in its entirety; the estate of Luciacum, in its entirety; half of the estate of Can; half of the estate of Beinis; and the two cultivated plots lying beside the aforesaid monastery within that forest, together with the meadow situated on the other side of the monastery, as the boundaries of those monks divide them; two small estates constructed beside the monastery above the river Sarthe; the estate of Salvaria with the other little estates adjoining it, with thirty resident dependents; and the demesne vineyard situated beside the monastery.

All this he transferred as a dowry to the aforesaid church and altar, for the monks serving God there according to the rule, with the consent of the most pious emperor Louis and of many bishops, especially those of the neighboring provinces, and of the clergy, and for the monks living there to possess perpetually.

He begged, testified, and humbly implored that no one remove these things from there, but rather increase and enlarge them; and just as each person wishes his pious deeds to remain stable, so may he permit our deeds, although small, to remain perpetually unshaken.

On that day and at that solemnity he decreed that the monks dwelling in that monastery and living according to the rule should provide a full meal to the canonical brothers serving the mother and senior church of the city; this will be recalled below.

He therefore judged that this meal should be given to the clerics serving the mother and senior church of the city. That church is likewise known to have been reconciled and solemnly consecrated, as has been specified, in honor of the Lord and Savior, of holy Mary, his mother, of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, and of Saint Stephen, and likewise in veneration and honor of all the saints, by the aforesaid Bishop Aldric.

In imitation and likeness of that church he consecrated this church in the aforementioned monastery. Since, therefore, it is subject to the mother and senior church of the city, he resolved to consecrate it in memory of those saints in whose honor the aforesaid mother church had been consecrated. This was accordingly carried out in an orderly and solemn manner, with the Lord’s help.

### XVIII

On the day of the consecration of the aforesaid church, as was mentioned above, he decreed that the aforementioned canons and servants of God, serving the mother and senior church—which the aforesaid Bishop Aldric built anew within the canons’ cloister—should receive the following provision from the estate already mentioned: from the monastery of Saint Savior, four modii of the best bread, three modii of the best wine, [an unclear quantity in the OCR] of the best drink, two wether *friscingae* [an uncertain food term], and likewise two pork ones.

He also decreed that the aforesaid canons should come in full and fitting procession, that is, with crosses and the remaining divine services and ornaments, as is proper for noble persons, to the Vespers and vigil of the aforesaid feast and dedication of the Lord Savior and of the church of that monastery.

[scan page 29]

Aldric of Le Mans

48

The canons of the city and all the suburban presbyters and clerics were to come, dressed for the occasion, in the morning at Prime, to the solemnity of the dedication of the church of Saint Stephen. Each priest was to sing one Mass in that church for the soul of the aforesaid Bishop Aldric; if he wished to do more, it was within his generosity and power.

Each cleric was to sing fifty psalms; if he wished to do more, it was within his generosity and mercy, without remuneration, praying and earnestly beseeching the Lord’s mercy that the soul of Bishop Aldric might enjoy eternal rest.

The office of the dedication of the church was to be celebrated fully, suitably, reasonably, and solemnly, together with the monks dwelling there and serving the Lord with the greatest devotion, according to what is found in the sacramentary, lectionary, antiphonary, and the other institutions of the holy Fathers, rationally arranged by prudent worshipers of the holy Church of God.

After Vespers, on the vigil of the dedication, the aforesaid canons were to have in the refectory, together with the monks, the same meal that the monks themselves had with them.

On the following day, after the Mass of the solemnity had been celebrated canonically and solemnly, the canons were to do whatever their bishop or masters judged better and more reasonably: either they were to dine fully in the monastery itself, or the aforesaid provisions were to be carried by their servants to their refectory, where they too were to dine fully and suitably, rejoicing and celebrating on account of the aforesaid solemnity.

### XIX

The aforesaid Aldric, bishop of the aforementioned city, also decreed and humbly requested that, on the day of the aforesaid solemnity, every priest of the city, every suburban priest, and every presbyter of the aforesaid monastery should celebrate one Mass for him while he lived in this present pilgrimage. After his death, whenever the Lord willed, he likewise decreed and earnestly requested, and enacted together with them, that on that day each of the aforesaid priests should devoutly sing one Mass for his soul.

The remaining clergy—that is, all the monks and canons—were each to sing fifty psalms with the greatest devotion, praying to the Lord of heaven that the aforesaid Aldric might be deemed worthy to have eternal life.

He likewise decreed that on the eleventh day before the Kalends of January, the dedication of the mother and senior church of the city, the priests and clerics should sing Masses and psalmody for Bishop Aldric with the same zeal as at the dedication of the church of Saint Savior in the aforesaid monastery: each priest one Mass, or more if he wished, and each cleric fifty psalms, or more if he desired, praying and beseeching the Lord of heaven that his soul might enjoy eternal life and deserve eternal rest. Amen.

### XX

Likewise, at the dedication of Saint Stephen, he decreed that the same should be done, so that he might deserve to have a share with the saints and chosen of God. Amen.

### XXI

The aforementioned lord Bishop Aldric, together with the brothers, fellow bishops, and canons of his see and church, also enacted the following.

He considered that on the day of his ordination all the presbyters, both urban and suburban, the monastic clergy, and the rest of the clergy should assemble together and solemnly at Vespers and at the vigil of that feast, just as it is prescribed to act on the birthdays of bishops. They were to perform those offices solemnly and devoutly with the canons, and, after Vespers had been completed, they were to drink three times in the refectory together with the canons of that church. Afterwards they were to come fully to Nocturns or Matins and solemnly and suitably perform the Matins office with the canons.

On the day of that solemnity he decreed and enacted, together with the wisest bishops and priests, that in the morning at Prime all the priests, urban and suburban alike, should assemble vested within the mother and senior church, and that the rest of the clergy should come with them.

Each presbyter was to devoutly sing three Masses for the aforesaid pontiff Aldric, and each cleric was to sing one psalter for himself; or the entire clergy together might sing one psalter antiphonally in the choir.

When these offices and Masses had been completed with the greatest devotion for Aldric, the venerable bishop, all were to enter together at the lawful and canonical hour into the public and solemn office, as it is prescribed to do on the birthdays of pontiffs.

After the public and solemn office had been performed, both the canons and all the clerics who had assembled to perform the aforesaid offices were to come together in the refectory and solemnly and sufficiently dine on the provision which the aforesaid Aldric had decreed should be given from the estate called Buxarias for the performance of those offices and completion of that solemnity, just as Bishop Aldric had established in the testament concerning that estate for the brothers, and as it was written and confirmed there by many bishops.

The aforesaid feast and the aforementioned meal of the brothers, which is now celebrated on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January, and which is advanced by one day because of the dedication of the aforesaid mother and

[scan page 30]

49

senior church of the city, were decreed and determined by the aforesaid Bishop Aldric and the aforementioned holy fellow bishops, priests, and all the canons to be transferred to the day of his deposition, when the Lord would wish to call him from this age.

On that day both the aforesaid meal and the aforementioned solemnity were to be celebrated. Whatever is now done for the living in Masses, psalmody, and the other prayers and ceremonies was then to be done likewise for the dead. After the prescribed number had been completed—that is, three Masses by each priest and one psalter by each cleric—it was to be carried out on the day of his deposition for the deceased bishop.

Then each person was to strive to act more devoutly and solemnly, because the need is greater then than now, since a friend who in life does not love a man’s soul after his death, and does not strive to pray for it, neglects and disdains to pray and strive for its rest.

For it has been considered and decreed by the aforesaid priests and servants of God that whoever neglects these things, or through whose negligence they are omitted, whether in giving the aforesaid provision or in performing the aforesaid offices, shall render an account of this before the tribunal of the strict Judge and shall receive his sentence there.

See to it, brothers and holy successors of the aforementioned bishop, that you do not neglect this decree, but rather strive to fulfill it, so that you may be able to receive not the punishment of condemnation but the reward of recompense forever. Amen.

Let us pray, brothers, that the Lord may grant the soul of the aforesaid pontiff Aldric a share in the first resurrection and permit him to have life in heaven, where, by his dispensation and gift, he may eternally deserve to enjoy everlasting glory together with the saints of God—he who lives and reigns with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, throughout infinite ages of ages. Amen.

### XXII

Likewise, at the feast of the dedication of the western part of the mother and senior church of the city, in which he built the altar of Saint John and three other altars, he decreed that the following be done.

Every priest, both urban and suburban, and all the monastic priests, were to assemble at that solemnity, which is on the eleventh day before the Kalends of July, vested and at Prime in the morning. There they were to celebrate one Mass for the aforesaid pontiff, Aldric, the venerable bishop; if they wished to do more, it was within their power and mercy, without remuneration.

Each cleric was to sing fifty psalms, or more, for the soul of Aldric, the aforesaid bishop, praying to the Lord of heaven and beseeching his mercy, so that the soul of the aforesaid Bishop Aldric might be able to possess eternal life and enjoy everlasting rest together with the saints and chosen of God throughout infinite ages of ages. Amen.

### XXIII

The aforesaid Aldric, the venerable bishop, also decreed that all the presbyters, urban, suburban, or monastic, living near the city, and all the priests dwelling within it, should assemble decently and vested at the following six feasts:

on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of September, when the feast of the Assumption of holy Mary, the mother of God, is celebrated;

at the feast of the consecration of the western part of the mother and senior church of the city, which is on the eleventh day before the Kalends of July;

at the feast of the dedication of the church of Saint Savior within the monastery of monks which the aforesaid Bishop Aldric founded anew above the river Sarthe, and in which he established monks to dwell and live according to the rule;

at the feast of the consecration of the church of Saint Stephen, which the aforesaid Bishop Aldric founded anew within the canons’ cloister, on the fifth day before the Ides of November;

at the feast of the birthday of the aforesaid Bishop Aldric, which is on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January, because it is advanced by one day, namely, the celebration of the consecration of the mother and senior church;

and at the feast of the consecration of the mother and senior church of the city, which is on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January.

For these feasts it was considered and decreed that the aforesaid priests should assemble vested at Prime in the morning, receive offerings and wine from the custodians of those churches, and perform the aforesaid offices for Bishop Aldric at Prime, before the third hour.

They were to pray humbly and supplicate, and, with bent knees, implore the Lord’s mercy—all the priests and all the remaining clerics alike—that the Lord absolve the soul of the aforesaid Bishop Aldric from every bond of sin, so that he might deserve to rise among the saints and chosen of God in the glory of the resurrection and enjoy eternal life with them throughout infinite ages of ages. Amen.

After these offices had been performed for the aforesaid Bishop Aldric with the greatest devotion and good will, all were to enter at the third hour into the public and solemn office of that day. When the solemn office had been suitably and solemnly completed, they were to have in the refectory, together with the canons of the aforesaid holy mother church, a full and fitting meal on each of the aforesaid six days and feasts.

They were to remain joyful, glad, and celebrating during those feasts, praising and blessing the Lord, who did not disdain to grant them such great benefits. They were also to continue in prayers and supplications to the Lord of heaven, so that they might be able to live this life peacefully, suitably, holily, and devoutly, and afterward, when God willed, might deserve to enjoy eternal life in the heavenly dwellings together with the saints of God. May he himself deign to grant this, to whom are honor and glory throughout the ages of ages. Amen.

Whoever desires to dissolve this arrangement, let him be separated from the members of the Church.

### XXIV

The aforesaid Bishop Aldric therefore built a monastery in the place where long ago a monastery had been constructed in honor of Saint Mary. He had acquired it, by legal title and through charter instruments, from the lord Emperor Louis for the right of the aforesaid church; but it was almost destroyed and ruined, and without...

[scan page 31]

**ALDRICI CENOMANENSIS EPISCOPI**

[The preceding sentence continues:] “...where the aforesaid monastery had formerly stood, that is, between the walls of the city and the Sarthe.” The aforesaid Bishop Aldric, as has been said, founded the monastery and endeavored to construct it anew as well as he could.

He built a church there larger than the one he had found destroyed, and consecrated it in honor of the Lord Savior, and of his holy mother Mary, the holy martyrs Stephen, Gervasius, and Protasius, on the eighth day before the Ides of October [8 October], with the canons and with solemn ceremonies.

He thought it proper to do this because the head of that monastery—the mother church of the city—had been consecrated in the name and honor of those saints, so that a member constructed there might preserve their memory and honor. Just as the aforesaid mother church had been dedicated in honor of the Lord Savior, holy Mary, and the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, so also the church in that monastery should be consecrated in the same way, so that the memory of those same saints might fittingly be venerated there in future times.

He therefore completed that church itself, namely, the refectory, dormitory, cells, and all the other structures belonging to a monastery; he arranged and adorned it nobly, and in the middle of the cloister caused a conduit to be made, so that water might flow from there through the cloister. In that monastery he also installed monks who lived according to the rule of Saint Benedict. With the permission of the lord Emperor Louis and of the lady Empress Judith, he transferred them there from the Imperial Monastery.

He decreed and confirmed this together with his metropolitan, his comprovincial bishops, and many other bishops, by the authority of the aforesaid Emperor Louis: that in future times monks should always remain there, living regularly and according to the rule of Saint Benedict; and if anyone should attempt to destroy or violate this arrangement—which God forbid—he should tremble before the tribunal of the judge and render an account.

He also gave the aforesaid monastery and the monks four villas, so that from them they might receive each year their stipends, clothing, and other necessities in full, and might live according to the rule without any impediment or want. These were: one villa at Laceriacum, in the county of Cenomanes, with complete possession; another in the county of Nivonense, with complete possession, called Taumiacus, situated on the Sarthe; a third on the same river Sarthe, called Monasteriolus; and a fourth in the county of Gabronense, called Cambron.

He determined that from the aforesaid monastery and from the aforesaid villas the ministers and monks of that monastery should provide one full and good meal each year to the canons living in the mother and senior church of the city, on the solemnity of the dedication of that church, namely on the fourth day before the Ides of October [12 October]. The canons, vested for the office of the dedication of that church, were to come there, and each year, as is contained in the order of the offices, the day was to be solemnly celebrated. There, that is, let each priest celebrate his Mass, and let each cleric chant fifty psalms [the intervening words are corrupt in the supplied scan], praying the Lord that they may deserve to obtain eternal life in heaven; moreover, chanting and most devoutly beseeching that God and the Lord may grant him eternal rest and perpetual light. Amen.

The aforesaid meal was to be of such a kind that the canons should receive each year six modii of the best grain, four modii of the best wine, four excellent *friscingae* of pork, and four modii of the best drink, both during the life of Aldric himself and after his death, so that they might always pray for him, both on that day and on the other days, and might devoutly celebrate the memory of his name, that he might deserve to rejoice and enjoy blessed and eternal rest with God’s saints in heaven. Amen.

### XXV

Bishop Aldric therefore entered the villa of his bishopric, namely in the county of Cenomanes, and established monks living according to the rule. He then arranged and completed the monastery as well as he could at that time; he built and consecrated the church and cloister, and prepared dwellings for monks who would live there according to the rule in future times.

He also decreed that monks should always remain there, praying for the lord emperor, for him, and for his successors, and should pray constantly for the Church of God, save their souls there, and win souls for God, while leading their life perpetually in that place according to the rule.

For these monks were part of his own see’s church and were assigned to it; and whatever was necessary for their value and for the completion and fulfillment of their services, he generously gave them from his own resources. At that time he transferred nothing from the monastery. Therefore, he wrote what follows in his own document, confirmed by the authority of the venerable bishops and of the other orders serving God, and likewise strengthened by the hands of laymen, religious persons, and nobles, and he handed it over with his own hands to be held and guarded in future times. Thus, from the properties inserted therein, they might supply their necessities, serve their lord and his successors regularly, win many for the Lord, and pray for the princes and pontiffs to whom they were subject, as well as for all the faithful of God’s holy churches in future times, so that through their prayers and those of other servants of God they might deserve to obtain forgiveness of all sins and everlasting life in heaven. Amen.

### XXVI

The aforesaid Aldric, bishop of the mother church of Cenomanes, built a certain monastery of monks in the county of Duciacum, at a place called Talipiacum, on the river Rhodanus, as well as the circumstances of that time permitted.

In the monastery of Talipiacum he built a church in honor of Saint Peter, together with a monks’ cloister, mills, and all the other buildings that seemed to belong to the care and rule of the monks, as well as the aforesaid bishop could construct them, and he nobly and wisely arranged and adorned them.

For the monastery of Talipiacum he sent monks from his own monastery, which is called Anisola, where the body of Saint Carilephus rests, so that they might live there regularly, pray incessantly day and night for all the sons of God’s holy Church, and win many for the Lord. They were to pray that our Lord and Savior, who redeemed us with his precious blood, might grant us to serve him faithfully day and night in many ways, to win many souls for God, to pray for Lord Louis the emperor and for his son Charles, and also for Bishop Aldric, for all entrusted to him, and for all the faithful of God’s holy Church; that he might grant us always to do his will, permit us to lead a happy life, and, through the merits of his servants and saints, deign to bring us into the fellowship of the saints. Amen.

In the aforesaid monastery of Talipiacum he appointed his provost, Jacob the archpriest, as abbot, so that he might oversee the monks there and govern them regularly according to the rule of Saint Benedict, and that he might save his own soul and the souls of others there, and lead them, with the Lord’s help, to the heavenly homeland, that is, to the celestial kingdom. May he deserve to reign and rejoice with them eternally in the heavenly dwellings together with God’s saints and elect, through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

He confirmed these villas and properties, mentioned above, to the aforesaid little monastery and to the monks serving God there, by his privilege, with the permission of the lord Louis, most pious emperor, and with the consent of Ursmar, his metropolitan, and of all his comprovincial holy bishops, with the assent also of the entire order and clergy entrusted to him—that is, of the whole body of priests, deacons, and other ministers of the sacred orders serving in the parish of Cenomanes.

### XXVII

The aforementioned Aldric, bishop of the mother church of Cenomanes, a pastor zealous for divine honor and moved by love, almost rebuilt from the foundations and endeavored to renew the monastery of Saint Vincent, situated beside the city of Cenomanes. He did not delay to adorn the church of Saint Vincent internally and externally with roofs and other buildings; on its northern side he constructed a monks’ cloister together with the other buildings that seemed to belong to their care and rule, as well as he could, and endeavored to arrange and adorn it nobly, wisely, and suitably.

In that aforesaid monastery of Saint Vincent, which he found almost destroyed and nearly abandoned, he placed monks after a large part had been rebuilt, so that they might live there according to the rule, attract many to the service of the Lord Savior and to the adornment of God’s holy Church, acquire many for the profit of souls and bodies and for the salvation and exaltation of the Christian people, and, living there holily, justly, piously, and regularly, win their own souls and the innumerable souls of others for the Lord.

They were to pray day and night for Lord Louis the emperor, for his wife Judith the empress, for their offspring, Charles the glorious king, and for all the flocks and peoples entrusted to them, faithfully imploring and asking that the Lord, our Savior, who redeemed us by his precious blood, grant us always to do his will, permit us to lead a happy life, and, through the intercession of his servants and the merits of God’s saints, deign to lead us into the fellowship of the saints. Amen.

### XXVIII

Record of the dwellings and newly cleared lands which the aforesaid Aldric, bishop of the city of Cenomanes, undertook to construct and clear for the benefit of God’s holy Church, the support of his servants, the sustenance of the poor and needy, the provision of those serving him, and the feeding or maintenance of livestock.

Beside the monastery of Saint Savior he made a dwelling for himself, and on Mount Seyaret he made eight small dwellings; in the properties of Vodebistria, three; in Ruiniacum, three; on the river Milicia, three; between Agniacum and the forest of Briscia, three; in Drumniacum, two; in Mantula, two belonging to Saint Mary; in Mantula of Saint Albin, one belonging to the brothers; in Novavilla, two; in Rino petroso, one; in Colonica beside the city, at the place called Vivariis, one; in Puscit, two; in that settlement beyond the river Sarthe, two; in that settlement of Saint Vincent, one; in Laudemaurum, one; in Bellatropia, three; in the forest of Laudensis, two; in the villa of Tricionis, five; on the river Liti beside Culturas, two; on the mountain of that villa, where the old vineyard stood, one; in the forest of Vaustina, seven; in Monciacum, three; in Canon, two; in Noiolium, one; in Vaustina, in the district of Vindonense, one; in the villa of Cipetra, on the river Sarthe, one; in Parciacum, one; in Casiliacum, two; in Aciacum, one; in Rupiacum, three; in the villa of the brothers at Aslnaria, two; in Colonica, two; in the old settlement, one; in Celsiacum, two; in Stauriaciacum, in the district of Baloca, two; in the forest of Blanau, in the district of Oxomensis, two; in Spelteriae, the villa of the brothers, two; in Calonica, two; in the old settlement, one; in Dumia, one; in Canania, three; and in Culcanna, or at Saint Julian, two.

Beside the monastery of Saint Carilephus, upon the great fishpond, one; at another monastery, one; at Belmont, a third; beside Maceriolae, four; beside the forest that Godefredus made, five; at Panitiaria, six; and seven in the field of Caballus; at Montcamp, ten; in the farm of Bovo, one; in the new villa, two; in Varinna, two; at Ruciacum, one; in Aldric’s wood, one; in Cipetum, on the river Lizi, at Belsa, one; in Pertica, at that cell, one; in Runviciacum, one; in Stiviale, one; at the dwellings beside the fork of Burgast, one; in Fraxinidum, at Belsa, in Vuodebris, one; beside Vuodebris, at the place called Saint Paternus, one; in Flaciacum, one; in Rufi ac um on the Sarthe, one; at Curtunvelt, one; in Brimum, one; in the villa of Maorana, one; in Breniacum, in the district of Bruslondense, one; in Brinnaicum, in the district of Exomensis, four; at Cerviae, one; at Curt Cardrici, one; at Piscosam, one; at Gaure, one; in Sarcinacum, on the river Meduana, one; in Cambion, one; in Boisingae, one; in Autlinga of Saxony, one; in Alona, one; beside the field of Sigelaicus, one; in Brisciola, one; in Molindareslingres, one; at Montmercant, one; in the territory of Cultures, above Truectum, on that mountain opposite Montcue, one; in the forest of Carnida, five; in Novavilla, in Audecavum, one; in the field of Seutdom, together with its church, one; in the cultivation called Monasteriolus, one; on the mountain at Archasum, beside Sabonaria, one; beside Proliacum of the robbers, one; in Contiliacum, one; in Contidia, one; at the villa of Huldwinus; and at Fraxinum, in the territory of Balian, one.

In all, 152 small dwellings were newly founded or rebuilt, a considerable number.

### XXIX

It seemed appropriate to insert into this little work copies of the privileges of the aforesaid bishop, and of the precepts obtained from emperors and kings by the aforesaid Bishop Aldric, with the purpose of strengthening those privileges, so that they might not be overturned by any contrivance. These privileges were confirmed by the authority of emperors and kings, and he made them for his monks and canons concerning certain properties and villas, so that they might receive their stipends in full and serve the Lord without want, while the mother church retained its privilege in full. Those wishing to know and investigate these matters will be able to find them in what follows.

#### Copy of the privilege made by the aforesaid pontiff for his brothers on the five festivals of the year and concerning the villa of Buxarias

In the name of Saint Savior and in veneration of holy Mary, God’s mother, and of the holy martyrs Stephen, Gervasius, and Protasius, whose church I appear, though unworthy, to be titular, I, Aldric, unworthy and sinful bishop of the city of Cenomanes, in the first year of my ordination, deeply saddened by the conduct of our brothers and canons, being one night engaged in prayer, as I believe, divinely inspired, began to consider how they might live more rationally and canonically, and how they might have a cloister—which, as is said, they had possessed for a long time, or rather had never possessed—in which they could live canonically and regularly, serving the Lord devoutly and religiously and canonically, and inhabiting it in the present and future.

At that time, with the consent of Landramnus, our venerable archbishop, and also at the request of all our comprovincial bishops, I gave to our aforesaid canons the house constructed on the right-hand and southern side of our see and mother church. It is consecrated in honor of Saint Savior and in the name and veneration of the aforesaid saints, namely holy Mary, God’s mother, the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, and Saint Stephen, and likewise in the veneration and name of all the saints. This was also the house in which my predecessors had formerly been accustomed to dwell.

Therefore I gave our aforesaid house and the aforesaid place, with all the buildings constructed upon and furnished with them, to our canons for habitation according to canonical order. I also took care to restore it, as far as the weakness of my strength permitted, in the manner of a cloister, and there I established them to live according to canonical institution and the order of the holy fathers, serving God and the aforesaid church canonically together, and all devoutly attending the canonical hours in the same manner. At the time of the meal, as the canonical order teaches, they were to come together for their nourishment in the refectory newly built through our labor, and were to receive everything that belonged to the support of the body in full, according to canonical order.

After this had been done, I humbly approached the clemency of our lord and senior, Louis, most pious emperor, asking him, as his most generous alms, to restore to me something from the properties of our see and mother church which the royal vassals held through his benefaction. With the Lord granting my request, he did not refuse it, but fulfilled my petition and confirmed it by his precept, sealed with his own ring.

When this had been faithfully done and obtained from his clemency, I asked him to grant me permission to give some of those properties, which had been restored to me, for the necessities of our brothers and canons. He did so.

Therefore, with a grateful heart, as an alms and in memory of the aforesaid lord Louis, most pious Augustus, I gave, with sound judgment and ready spirit, to the aforesaid brothers and canons, together with the consent of the aforesaid Lord Landramnus, archbishop of the church of Tours, and of all our other comprovincial bishops, for the support of our aforesaid brothers and canons, in the county of Cenomanes, within the aforesaid city, a villa named Buxarias with everything belonging to it, and a forest called Follicionis, with complete possession. Through this testament I confirmed these properties for the increase of their support in future times.

I did this so that each year the aforesaid brothers might receive from the aforesaid villa, on the feast of the dedication of the western part of the mother and senior church, which falls on the eleventh day before the Kalends of July [21 June], where on that same western side there is a consecrated altar in honor of Saint John, two other altars in honor of other saints whose names are written above those altars, and a fourth altar constructed above in the upper chamber, consecrated on that day in honor of all the saints, the following provisions.

On the aforesaid eleventh day before the Kalends of July, in honor of the aforesaid dedication and solemnity, we establish and decree by this testament—and, with the counsel and exhortation of many bishops and priests, devoutly establish—that our aforesaid canons and brothers receive:

- six modii of the best grain;
- four modii of the best wine;
- one modius of the drink commonly called *alixona*;
- four excellent rams;
- two excellent pigs.

At the dedication of the church of Saint Stephen, which is built within the cloister and whose dedication feast falls on the ninth day before the Ides of November [5 November], the brothers shall likewise receive:

- six modii of the best grain;
- four modii of the best wine;
- one modius of the drink called *silvia*;
- two very good *friscingae* of pork;
- four rams.

On the anniversary of our ordination, which falls on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January [21 December], but which is advanced by one day because of the dedication of the mother and senior church of our see, which falls on the eleventh day before the Kalends of January [22 December], the aforesaid brothers shall receive for their meal:

- six modii of the best grain;
- four modii of the best wine;
- one modius of fennel drink;
- five solidi for the purchase of fish;
- one modius of cheese;
- likewise one modius of the best legumes.

At the dedication of the apse of the mother and senior church of our city, and at the reconciliation of that church, which I have newly built and endeavored to rebuild, and which I solemnly dedicated on the eleventh day before the Kalends of January [22 December] in honor of Saint Savior and in the name of holy Mary, God’s mother, the holy martyrs Stephen, Gervasius, and Protasius, and likewise in honor and veneration of all the saints, together with many other bishops and priests, and in which I placed relics of many saints with my own hands—including relics of the bodies of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, which I fittingly arranged when dedicating the relics in the confession of the principal altar—the aforesaid brothers shall receive on that feast:

- six modii of the best grain;
- four modii of the best wine;
- one modius of the best *costum* [an aromatic substance; reading uncertain];
- five solidi for the purchase of fish;
- one modius of cheese;
- likewise one modius of legumes.

All these provisions shall be supplied from the aforesaid villa of Buxarias to the aforesaid brothers with the greatest devotion, as has been specified.

We decreed that these things should be given to them for this reason: so that on the aforesaid five festivals the brothers might solemnly and devoutly celebrate them together with all the monasterial clergy, suburban priests, and other clerics who should come with the greatest devotion to the vigils of the aforesaid festivals. Then, in the morning at Prime, vested, they should devoutly be present in the church whose feast is being celebrated. The custodian of that church shall provide them sufficiently with offerings and wine at each altar, so that, for me, a sinful man, while I live, each priest may celebrate one Mass, and more if he wishes and charity supplies it; and each cleric may chant fifty psalms, or more, as affection and the love of God may inspire him.

The canons themselves and the suburban or monastic clerics of the other choir should take care to chant these psalms in turn in the aforesaid church.

After my death, when God wills, on the aforesaid festivals and at the appointed times, they shall likewise do these things humbly for the deceased, both in Masses and in psalmody, as we earnestly ask.

When all this has been carefully done, at the third hour they shall enter the public office and celebrate the solemnity of that day. After the office of the aforesaid feast has been solemnly completed, they shall then eat religiously in the refectory together with the aforesaid monastic and suburban priests and clerics, listening continually and attentively to a reading, and being most religiously refreshed in silence.

I therefore earnestly and humbly beseech my holy successors, and the superiors, masters, or ministers of the aforesaid canons, whether the present canons or those of the future, not to exclude from the aforesaid meal and from their refectory the suburban or monastic priests and clerics who come to the aforesaid feast and offer the prayers written above for me, the most wretched sinner.

But if this should happen because of some necessity, then, establishing this arrangement, we implore that one of the canons, a thoroughly faithful man, should take from the stipends granted from the aforesaid villa of Buxarias one modius of bread and another of wine, together with four sextarii of the aforesaid drink and one *friscinga*, whichever he finds better, and should prepare from these, within the appointed cloister and in the best place, a full meal for them devoutly and religiously.

But I much prefer, and humbly beseech, that they eat with our aforesaid canons in the refectory, conducting the aforesaid days solemnly with them, rejoicing in such great feasts, and praising and beseeching God in all things, so that they may be able to lead this life in tranquility and deserve to receive the rewards of eternal life.

Moreover, concerning the aforesaid stipends, I appeal to my holy successors and ministers of the aforesaid mother church, and humbly beseech them, that at each of the aforesaid festivals they give one modius of the designated bread, another of the aforesaid wine, and one of the aforesaid *friscingae* to forty poor people, and prepare a meal for them from these provisions in the best place. Having received the meal, may they rejoice in the Lord Savior, and endeavor to pray for me, the most wretched sinner, living and dead, so that I may rejoice eternally with God’s saints and elect and deserve to enjoy perpetual life. Amen.

Whatever more is produced or acquired in the aforesaid villa than has been inserted above as to be supplied at the aforesaid festivals, through any just skill or craft, shall come to the common benefit of the aforesaid brothers and shall contribute to the increase of their meals. Nothing from the resources of the aforesaid villa shall be taken away from them or diminished by anyone, so that they may be increasingly able to fulfill the service of almighty God and to pray humbly for the perpetuity of the empire and for our aforesaid lord and senior Louis, most pious emperor, for the safety of his wife and offspring, and for the victorious triumph of his invincible army.

I therefore earnestly beseech all who succeed me in this see, as though prostrate at their feet, to preserve permanently this arrangement which, for love of the Lord Savior and in veneration of holy Mary, God’s mother, the holy martyrs Stephen, Gervasius, and Protasius, and all the saints, and as an alms of the aforesaid Emperor Louis, with his permission and for the burden of my sins, I have decreed should be made and remain forever.

If anyone should presume to violate this devotion, let him bring a trembling account before the tribunal of Christ, for whose love this is known to have been done.

I, Aldric, unworthy and sinful bishop of the city of Cenomanes, have subscribed this testament made by me.

I, Ursmar, unworthy archbishop of the city of Tours, agreeing to this testament, have subscribed.

I, Dodo, humble bishop of the Andegavian people, have given my assent to this decree of the testament and subscribed.

I, Jonas, unworthy bishop, agreeing to this testament, have subscribed.

I, Autcarius, archbishop of the city of Mainz, have subscribed.

I, Ebroinus, unworthy bishop, agreeing to this testament, have subscribed.

I, Guntardus, unworthy bishop, agreeing to this testament, have subscribed.

I, Erchenradus, bishop of the city of Paris, at the request of Bishop Aldric, have subscribed this testament.

I, Varnarius, unworthy bishop, have subscribed this testament.

I, Echardus, bishop, at the request of Bishop Aldric, have subscribed this testament.

Theodoricus, bishop of the city of Cambrai, have subscribed this testament.

David, chorbishop, have subscribed.

Ansteus, dean, have subscribed.

Godinus, archpriest, have subscribed.

Ricardus, priest, have subscribed.

Dedivinus, archpriest, have subscribed.

Eruardus, though unworthy, priest, have subscribed.

Geraldus have subscribed.

Gansuinus, priest, have subscribed.

Ascaricus, priest, have subscribed.

Alexander, priest, have subscribed.

Gerihanus, priest, have subscribed.

Vineboldus, priest, have subscribed.

Plodoinus, priest, have subscribed.

Plodebertus, priest, have subscribed.

Anisacharus, deacon, have subscribed.

Rodricus, deacon, have subscribed.

Regnogardus, notary, have subscribed.

Vivaldus, subdeacon, have subscribed.

Given on the Kalends of April [1 April], on Holy Easter Day, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 837, in the fifteenth indiction, in the twenty-third year of the reign of our lord Louis, most glorious emperor, and in the fifth year of our ordination. Done publicly in the city of Cenomanes, successfully, in the name of God. Amen.

### XXX

#### Copy of the imperial precept of Louis concerning the aforesaid privilege of the villa of Buxarias

In the name of our Lord God and Savior Jesus Christ.

I, Louis, by the favor of divine clemency Emperor Augustus, make known to all the holy Church of God and to our faithful, present and future, that the venerable man Aldric, bishop of the city of Cenomanes, our subject, represented to our gentleness that at the beginning of his ordination he had found the order and condition of the canons of the mother church entrusted to him in confusion, and that they had hitherto possessed no cloister in which they ought to live canonically.

Burning with love of the divine service, he had therefore assigned to the dwellings of the aforesaid canons the houses which his predecessors as bishops had been accustomed to keep for their own use. After constructing, furnishing, and adorning those buildings according to the needs of each use, he had made the canons dwell there according to canonical authority.

He also reported to our serenity that, by adding certain oratories and other churches outside the walls to the aforesaid mother church, he had taken care to fulfill their devotion solemnly and religiously, so that the aforesaid canons might celebrate the feasts of those dedications solemnly at their appointed times, with priests, religious laymen, and the remaining people assembling together.

He had assigned to those canons, by a testament written and confirmed by his own venerable hands and those of the other bishops, a certain villa called Buxarias, so that on the aforesaid festivals of the dedications, under certain stipulated conditions, they might receive a worthy and necessary meal.

He therefore entreated our highness that, so that his institution might remain inviolable for all time, he might deserve to receive the authority of our confirmation for the strengthening of what he had most devoutly and religiously established, through which it might remain undisturbed and inviolable in future times.

Granting his petitions, by this writing of our authority we establish and decree that what he is known to have done and instituted zealously for the honor and worship of God, and what he did not delay to have written and confirmed in the series of his aforesaid document, shall remain undisturbed for all time.

None of his successors shall dare to alter anything of the conditions contained therein or to withdraw the aforesaid villa from the right of those same canons. Rather, whatever the aforesaid canons wish to order and arrange concerning it according to his institution, as has been said, they shall have free power in all things, so that they may continually be able to implore the mercy of the Lord for us, for our wife and offspring, and for the stability of the entire empire granted to us by God.

And so that the authority of this confirmation of ours may retain inviolable and unshaken force in our times and those of our successors, we have ordered it to be sealed below with our ring.

Hirminmarus, notary, have examined and subscribed on behalf of Hugo.

Given on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of July [18 June], in the twenty-third year, Christ being favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the fifteenth indiction. Done at the villa of Thionville, in the royal palace, successfully, in the name of God. Amen.

### XXXI

What follows is a copy of the privilege made by the aforementioned Aldric, bishop of the church of Saint Savior on the river Sarthe, for the monks serving the Lord there.

In the name of the holy Trinity and the one Divinity,

I, Aldric, unworthy and sinful bishop of the city of Cenomanes, moved by divine illumination and the inspiration of pious compassion...

### [Scan page 36]

… together with the most pious emperor Louis, and with all the bishops of the neighboring provinces and of many other provinces, noble and learned pontiffs, and with all our congregation devoted to God, together with the mother church of our see. I, considering the weakness of human frailty and trembling at the final day of my vocation, lest—burdened with a great weight of sins—I should be found, God forbid, without any fruit of good works, and encouraged by the words of the chief preacher, namely the Apostle Paul, where he says, “If anyone’s work endures, he shall receive a reward,” therefore, as has been said, with the consent and permission of the aforesaid prince and of the aforesaid holy bishops and servants of God, with a most willing spirit, divine clemency inspiring me, I resolved in the compunction of my devotion that, for the increase of divine worship and of the church of the holy mother and of our see, and of the parish entrusted to us, and for the accumulation of honor and the salvation of many souls, we should found and build by our labor a certain small monastery in our parish, for the perpetual praise of almighty God.

With the Lord’s approval we have endeavored to do this. In it we have also caused a church to be built, insofar as our ability permitted, and to be perpetually dedicated to the name of the eternal God, in honor of the Lord Savior and of holy Mary, the same Mother of God, and of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius and of Saint Stephen, and also in honor and memory of all the saints. On the sixteenth day before the Kalends of October, together with the other bishops and priests, and with the remaining ministers of the holy Church of God, we took care to consecrate it decently, reasonably, canonically, and solemnly, with the Lord’s help.

In it we also raised fifteen altars in honor and memory of those saints whose names now appear inscribed upon them. With my own hands I placed there their patronages and relics, and, solemnly and decently, together with the most holy associates mentioned above, whom the Lord in his mercy permitted us to have, I consecrated and sanctified them in due order. We humbly ask that, through the intercessions of these saints, we may mercifully be helped and protected by their perpetual patronage, the Lord granting this.

Therefore, on the aforesaid day of the Kalends and at the dedication of the aforesaid church, with the permission and exhortation of the aforementioned prince and of the aforesaid holy fathers—namely the bishops and the noble and holy-living priests—we handed over and assigned, in the presence and sight of many nobles, through a finely ornamented Gospel book partly written in gold, and through one golden chalice with its paten placed above it, while the bishops and priests laid their hands upon them, together with the aforesaid Gospel book and the aforementioned golden chalice, certain possessions of the church of our holy see to the aforesaid holy place called the monastery of Saint Savior, formerly Brogilus, for the use of the monks living there according to the rule and serving the Lord.

We have given and donated these possessions there in perpetuity, for the reward and stability of our aforesaid lord Louis, the most pious emperor, through whose generosity we have been worthy to acquire the aforesaid place, and also for the future benefit of his successors, namely the kings of the Franks, and for the benefit of our successors. Through this testament we give and confirm them, and wish them to remain confirmed for all future time, both for the needs and for the pious support of the brothers serving the Lord there, and also for the reception and assistance of pilgrims and arriving guests.

First, we assigned there the estate of Salvarias, with thirty manses, and two small cultivated plots situated beside that monastery; also the wood lying between the river Sarthon and the aforesaid cultivated lands and the monastery; likewise the lordly vineyard adjoining Salvarias and the aforesaid monastery; and two mills situated beside that monastery above the river Sarthon; and also the meadow situated on the other side of the aforesaid monastery, together with its wood, according to the boundaries by which the lands of the aforesaid monks are divided.

We also assigned there the estate of our see’s church called Apiacum, in its entirety, where Saint Ulfacius, the precious confessor of Christ, rests bodily. At the same time we handed over half of the estate called Canon. In the same way we confirm there the estate of Luciacum in its entirety. We also gave there half of the estate called Bernas, belonging to Saint Mary, which we acquired through the restitution of our lord Louis, the most excellent emperor.

We likewise hand over in its entirety the precarium which Friderardus holds by precarial tenure from the possessions of Saint Mary and Saint Gervasius, and we donate it in the same way. In the estate called Saint Autien, we give the three inhabitants with their three vineyards and other fields, together with whatever part of Saint Mary’s property is held there.

We confirm through this testament the possessions which Saleardus lawfully handed over there to the same holy place, to us, or to the monks themselves on the day of the dedication of that church. All these things are situated in the county of Cenomanicum.

Therefore, all the aforesaid estates and all the possessions mentioned above, and everything legally belonging to those estates, together with the other houses, buildings, dependants, vineyards, woods, fields, meadows, pastures, waters and watercourses, mills, movable and immovable property—in short, everything and from everything—we donate, hand over, and assign to the aforesaid holy place, for the acquisition of holy reward and for the increase of the church of our holy see and for the adornment of our congregation.

Whatever divine mercy may thereafter wish to increase for that most holy place and for the brothers and monks serving the Lord there and living according to the rule, and whatever good people may donate and hand over there, let all of it, with the Lord’s help, perpetually prosper there from this day forward. For this reason, moved by pious devotion, I have established that, on the anniversary of the consecration of the church of the aforesaid Saint Savior, consolation shall every year be provided to the brothers serving the mother church and the church of our see by the abbot and monks serving the Lord in the aforesaid monastery: namely, six measures of the best bread, three pork flitches, likewise three portions of mutton, four measures of the best wine, and five measures of the best drink.

We have decreed that these things should be given to them so that the aforesaid canons of the mother church may come fully to the celebration of the dedication of the aforesaid church, with silence and the other divine ornaments, together with the other suburban priests and the remaining clergy. Then, in the morning at Prime, each priest shall sing one Mass there for me, a sinner, as long as I live, and more if he has the means and charity permits; and each cleric shall recite fifty psalms, and more insofar as devotion and the love of God may urge him.

After my death, on the aforesaid day, let them do the same for me as a dead man. When all these things have been carefully completed, at the third hour let them enter the public office, and together with the monks serving the Lord there let them solemnly celebrate the festal solemnity of that day. Then let them do whichever they choose: either dine there together with those monks, or, if they do not dine there, let them take the allowance and dine in the refectory within the house and cloister of the canons, together with the aforesaid suburban priests, clerics, and priests.

I humbly entreat my holy successors, and the abbots or monks of the aforesaid monastery, and the provosts, masters, or ministers of our canons, as well as the canons themselves, present and future, and the aforesaid suburban priests, and the monastic priests and clerics who come to the aforesaid celebration and perform the prayers written above for me, the most wretched sinner: let them not exclude them from the aforesaid meal or from their refectory.

But if this should happen because of some necessity, then we implore them to establish that one trustworthy canon, from the allowances which the aforesaid monks have provided, shall receive one measure of bread and another of wine, together with four sextaries of drink and one pork flitch, whichever he finds to be the best, and shall devoutly and religiously prepare a meal from these provisions for those men.

But I prefer and earnestly entreat that they dine with our aforesaid canons in the refectory, in the most religious manner, celebrating that day with them, rejoicing in so great a festival, and praising and beseeching the Lord in all things that they may be able to lead a peaceful life and may deserve to receive the rewards of eternal life.

Moreover, from the aforesaid allowances, I beseech my holy successors and, beseeching them, humbly entreat the ministers of the same church to give one measure of the prescribed bread, another of the aforementioned wine, and one of the aforesaid pork flitches to forty poor persons at the aforesaid celebration. Having received a meal from these provisions, may they praise the Lord Savior of the world together and strive to pray for me, the most wretched sinner, so that we may deserve to rejoice eternally with the saints and elect of God. Amen.

Furthermore, although we see many episcopal sees and mother churches possessing various monasteries built under their authority, I ask that no one assert that I have done this superfluously—especially since I confess that I have done it more for the honor of the church entrusted to us and for the profit of souls than for any human undertaking. Nor is it surprising that I have enriched the aforesaid place with the possessions of our church’s see, since we read and know that many holy bishops have already done similar things.

Therefore I ask all the faithful of the holy Church of God not to think that I have done this superfluously, but rather not to disdain praying for me, a sinner, so that, if I have deserved to obtain any reward for this, they may deserve to become participants in it.

Finally, I humbly entreat our Lord Jesus Christ, my blessed successor who will soon be appointed, and all the bishops who will succeed him in the see entrusted to us; and, as though prostrate at their feet, I earnestly implore all princes, nobles and non-nobles, and all Christians, to preserve the small work undertaken by us for the divine praise of almighty God and for the increase of the aforesaid little monastery of Saint Savior. For the sake of their alms, and for love of the aforesaid Lord Savior—in whose honor the aforesaid little monastery is known to have been built and dedicated—may they deign to increase its possessions.

Let them not presume to diminish or withdraw from what we have done and assigned there, so that their good deeds, both in the present and in the future, as well as ours, may, with God’s protection, be preserved. Thus, if we have deserved to receive any reward for this pious deed, with the Lord’s approval, may we deserve—through the aid of that same Lord Savior, for whose love we have done this—to become sharers in that reward.

I also entreat all priests and servants of God, and all monks, to take care to fulfill the aforesaid prayers for me, a sinner, on the aforesaid day, piously and with the greatest zeal, so that, through their prayers, I may obtain absolution from all my sins, and, with the Lord’s granting, may we perpetually enjoy the fellowship of the saints.

Likewise, I earnestly entreat all the abbots and monks living in the aforesaid monastery of Saint Savior not to neglect supplying the aforesaid allowances to our canons and brothers, or to the suburban priests and clerics, on the aforesaid day. Thus, while they supply these things, while we humbly serve, and while the other brothers and servants of God pray, may Jesus Christ our Lord deign to cherish us and them in eternal joy together with his saints. Amen.

Furthermore, so that this testament or privilege, made by me with pious intention, may remain unviolated and most firm for all time, we have strengthened it with our own hand for the sake of firmness. We have also humbly requested our holy fathers, the bishops, and our priestly brothers and deacons, as well as the other clerics and the remaining persons whose names are written below, to confirm it with their signatures.
